cards.rueckseite:
**Infants (< 2 y):** mostly **supratentorial** (teratoma, embryonal tumors, choroid plexus tumors, DIG).
**Children 4–11 y:** mostly **infratentorial** (pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, ependymoma, brainstem glioma).
**Adults:** ~70% supratentorial; **metastases** outnumber primaries clinically; most common primaries: meningioma, glioblastoma. Most common primary posterior fossa tumor in adults: **hemangioblastoma** (after metastases).
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 210–211. In children, brain tumors are the second most common cancer after leukemia (most common solid tumors).

zeilen: Neuronal/neuroendocrine: ganglioglioma, central neurocytoma, medulloblastoma, pituitary adenoma, paraganglioma
Carcinoma, chordoma, craniopharyngioma, choroid plexus tumors
Hemangioblastoma stromal cells (EMA negative, unlike renal cell carcinoma)
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 211–212; updated markers per WHO CNS5 (2021).

zeilen: Nuclei around a central tangle of fibrillary processes (no lumen)
Columnar cells around a true central lumen
Cells with fibrillary processes radiating to a vessel

cards.vorderseite: WHO CNS5 (2021): adult diffuse glioma classification
cards.rueckseite:
- **Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant** (grade 2–4; ATRX loss, TP53; grade 4 if **CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion** or necrosis/MVP)
- **Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted** (grade 2–3)
- **Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype** (grade 4): or IDH-wt diffuse astrocytoma with **TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification or +7/−10** ("molecular GBM")
cards.notiz: WHO CNS5 2021; CNBR p. 213–222 uses the 2016 scheme.

cards.rueckseite:
Histology: hypercellular, pleomorphic astrocytic tumor with **pseudopalisading necrosis** and **microvascular (endothelial) proliferation**, mitoses.
Markers: **EGFR amplification**, PTEN loss, TERT promoter mutation, +7/−10. **MGMT promoter methylation** predicts benefit from temozolomide (better survival). Variants: gliosarcoma, giant cell GBM, epithelioid GBM (BRAF V600E).

WHO grade 1. **Biphasic** pattern: compact areas with bipolar "hair-like" (piloid) cells and **Rosenthal fibers**, alternating with loose microcystic areas with **eosinophilic granular bodies**. Vascular proliferation and degenerative atypia do **not** imply malignancy. Molecular: **KIAA1549–BRAF fusion** (cerebellum), BRAF V600E; NF1 (optic pathway).

"**Fried egg**" cells (perinuclear halos, a formalin fixation artifact, absent on frozen section), "**chicken-wire**" capillaries, microcalcifications (~80% calcify), perineuronal satellitosis. Frontal lobe, cortical involvement.
Definition: **IDH mutation + 1p/19q codeletion** → chemosensitive (PCV), best prognosis among diffuse gliomas.

Diffuse glioma in **thalamus, brainstem (pons, previously DIPG), spinal cord** or other midline sites with **H3 K27M** mutation/loss of H3K27me3. WHO grade 4 regardless of histology. Children > adults. Not resectable (pons); radiotherapy; median survival ~1 year.

**Perivascular pseudorosettes** (most typical), true ependymal rosettes, blepharoplasts; GFAP+, **EMA dot-like/ring** positivity.
WHO CNS5 groups by site: supratentorial **ZFTA (RELA) fusion** or YAP1 fusion; posterior fossa **PFA** (infants, poor) / **PFB** (adults, better); spinal (MYCN-amplified aggressive); **myxopapillary** (filum, now grade 2); **subependymoma** (grade 1, older men, 4th/lateral ventricle).

**Papilloma (grade 1):** fibrovascular cores lined by a single layer of cuboidal/columnar epithelium; children → **lateral ventricle (atrium)**, adults → **4th ventricle**; hydrocephalus from CSF overproduction. Cytokeratin, transthyretin, S-100 positive.
**Carcinoma (grade 3):** young children, invasion, necrosis; associated with **Li–Fraumeni (TP53)**.

**Ganglioglioma:** dysplastic neurons + neoplastic glia, **temporal lobe**, children/young adults, **chronic epilepsy**; cyst with enhancing mural nodule, calcification; **BRAF V600E** (~20–60%), CD34+.
**DNET (dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor):** cortical, multinodular, "bubbly" T2, little enhancement, **specific glioneuronal element** with **floating neurons** in mucoid matrix; epilepsy surgery cures seizures; FGFR1 alterations.

Young adults; **lateral ventricle near the foramen of Monro**, attached to the septum pellucidum; "bubbly" calcified mass. Uniform round cells with perinuclear halos (oligodendroglioma-like) but **synaptophysin positive** (neuronal), GFAP negative. WHO grade 2; gross total resection usually curative.

Small round blue cell tumor, **Homer Wright rosettes**, synaptophysin+; vermis/4th ventricle in children, CSF seeding.
Groups: **WNT** (best prognosis, CTNNB1, monosomy 6, older children), **SHH** (infants and adults, desmoplastic/nodular; **Gorlin syndrome (PTCH1)**, TP53-mutant = poor), **group 3** (MYC amplification, worst), **group 4** (most common, isochromosome 17q).

Infants (< 3 y), posterior fossa or supratentorial; rhabdoid cells with eccentric nuclei and eosinophilic inclusions, polyphenotypic IHC. **Loss of INI1 (SMARCB1, 22q11)** nuclear staining (rarely SMARCA4). WHO grade 4, poor prognosis; can mimic medulloblastoma.

From **arachnoid cap cells** (arachnoid granulations). **Whorls** and **psammoma bodies**; EMA and SSTR2A positive, vimentin+, PR often positive. Subtypes: meningothelial, **transitional (most common)**, fibrous, psammomatous (spinal), secretory, angiomatous.
Risk factors: **ionizing radiation**, **NF2 (chromosome 22)**, female hormones (progesterone receptors; grow in pregnancy).

zeilen: 4–19 mitoses/10 HPF **or brain invasion** or ≥ 3 of: sheeting, small cells, macronucleoli, hypercellularity, spontaneous necrosis; clear cell, chordoid subtypes
≥ 20 mitoses/10 HPF, frank anaplasia, **TERT promoter mutation or CDKN2A/B deletion**; (rhabdoid, papillary graded by criteria in CNS5)

cards.rueckseite: **Ipsilateral optic atrophy** (direct compression) + **contralateral papilledema** (raised ICP) ± anosmia. Classic for **olfactory groove / sphenoid wing meningioma** (frontal base mass).

Dural-based, mimics meningioma but: "**staghorn**" vessels, no whorls/psammoma bodies, **EMA negative**, **CD34 and nuclear STAT6 positive** (**NAB2–STAT6 fusion**). High recurrence and **extracranial metastasis** (bone, lung, liver) → resection + radiotherapy, long-term follow-up.

WHO grade 1. Capillary network with **lipid-laden vacuolated stromal cells** (the neoplastic cell; inhibin-α, S-100, NSE positive; **EMA negative**, keratin negative → distinguish from metastatic **renal cell carcinoma**). ~25–30% with **VHL** (3p25). Cyst with mural nodule (cerebellum); can produce **erythropoietin** → polycythemia.

**Adamantinomatous:** children (also older adults), **calcified, cystic** ("motor oil" fluid), palisading basal cells, stellate reticulum, **wet keratin**; **CTNNB1 (β-catenin) mutation**, nuclear β-catenin.
**Papillary:** adults, solid, rarely calcified, no wet keratin; **BRAF V600E** (targetable).
Both WHO grade 1 but locally aggressive.

cards.notiz: CNBR p. 241–243. Germinoma = most common pineal tumor (~40%); pineal in males, suprasellar in females; very radiosensitive.

cards.rueckseite:
**Pineocytoma** (grade 1): adults, slow, **large pineocytomatous rosettes**.
**Pineal parenchymal tumor of intermediate differentiation** (grade 2–3).
**Pineoblastoma** (grade 4): children, small round blue cells, Homer Wright/Flexner–Wintersteiner rosettes; **trilateral retinoblastoma** = bilateral retinoblastoma + pineoblastoma (RB1, DICER1).

From **notochord remnants**: clivus and **sacrum** (most common), rarely mobile spine. **Physaliphorous cells** (bubbly vacuolated cytoplasm) in myxoid matrix. Positive: **brachyury**, cytokeratin, EMA, S-100. Chondroid chordoma variant; differential: chondrosarcoma (brachyury and keratin negative, petroclival off-midline).

Mostly **diffuse large B-cell lymphoma** (CD20+), **angiocentric** growth (perivascular cuffing, reticulin "onion-skin"). Periventricular/deep, homogeneous enhancement, restricted diffusion. Immunocompromised: EBV-associated, ring enhancing. **Avoid steroids before biopsy** (tumor "vanishes"). Treatment: high-dose methotrexate-based chemotherapy, not resection.

- **Anti-Hu (ANNA-1):** small cell lung cancer → sensory neuronopathy, limbic/brainstem encephalitis
- **Anti-Yo (PCA-1):** ovarian/breast cancer → **cerebellar degeneration**
- **Anti-Ri:** breast → opsoclonus–myoclonus
- **Anti-Ma2:** testicular → limbic/brainstem encephalitis
- **Anti-NMDA receptor:** ovarian teratoma → psychiatric symptoms, dyskinesias, seizures
- **VGCC antibodies:** SCLC → Lambert–Eaton

**Epidermoid:** stratified squamous epithelium with **dry keratin** ("pearly tumor"), **off-midline** (CPA, parasellar), insinuates around vessels/nerves; **DWI bright** (restricted), FLAIR not suppressed. Rupture → chemical meningitis.
**Dermoid:** also dermal appendages (hair, sebaceous glands), **midline**, fat signal (T1 bright); associated with dermal sinus; rupture → fat droplets in the subarachnoid space.

Anterior **third ventricle** at the foramen of Monro; endodermal origin; ciliated columnar epithelium with mucin (PAS+), CT **hyperdense**. Can cause **sudden death** (acute obstructive hydrocephalus); positional headaches. Treatment: endoscopic or transcallosal/transcortical resection.

**Rathke cleft cyst:** remnant of Rathke pouch, intra/suprasellar between anterior and posterior lobe; **single layer of ciliated cuboidal/columnar epithelium**, mucoid content, **no calcification, no solid enhancing component** (thin rim only), intracystic waxy nodule on MRI.
Craniopharyngioma: calcification, solid enhancing parts, keratin.
